title: SLO thermostat cohort experiment notes
content:
Purpose:
Run a targeted experiment (we're calling it the 'SLO thermostat') to observe how cohort-aware routing + adaptive batching affects end-to-end latency quantiles and per-stage contribution across realistic traffic slices. Goal is to produce an actionable plan that gets p95 under 350ms for the text-generation route while keeping p99 regression <= 5% relative to baseline.

Context / motivating incident:
- Week-over-week we've seen p95 regressions on route /v1/generate for some customers after the autoscaler bump (see INF-2487).
- Topline suspicion: increased burstiness caused more cross-cohort mixing in batcher, causing larger batching wait times for long-seq requests and evicting caches causing model-run stalls.

Experiment design (high level):
1) Create 4 cohorts by request characteristics: short (<=32 tokens), medium (33-128), long (129-512), streaming (chunked incremental).
2) For each cohort, route to: baseline pool (current), thermostat pool A (capped concurrency, prefer short-run), thermostat pool B (isolated long-run), and fallback pool (cheaper quantized model).
3) Collect E2E traces for 48 hours, sample 1 in 100 requests, aggregate p50/p95/p99 per-cohort and per-stage.
4) Compare stage breakdown: tokenization, prefix-parse, kv-cache-lookup, model-infer (kernel time), batcher-wait, emit/egress.

Sampling and instrumentation details:
- Trace sampler: slo-therm-sampler v0.2 (attached via tracing config INF-2487).
- Sampling rate: 1% global + targeted 5% on p99 tail via tail-sampler rule.
- Trace fields captured: route, model_variant, seq_len_estimate, batch_size_at_send, kv_cache_hit(bool), start_ts, stage timestamps (tokenize_start, model_start, model_end, emit_done).
- Representative trace ids (for quick lookup): trace-20251112-9a1b, trace-20251113-c3f9, trace-20251114-f72e.

Aggregate results (48h, cohorted):
NOTE: numbers are median of runs; raw numbers in linked artifact (GH PR + attached csv).

Cohort: short (<=32) - 45% of traffic
- E2E p50: 82ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 285ms
- Per-stage median fraction (p95 sample): tokenization 8%, prefix-parse 5%, kv-cache 3% (mostly hits), model-infer 58%, batcher-wait 20%, emit/egress 6%
- Observation: batcher-wait correlates with spikes when medium cohort is present in pool.

Cohort: medium (33-128) - 35% of traffic
- E2E p50: 140ms, p95: 320ms, p99: 620ms
- Per-stage fraction (p95 sample): tokenization 7%, prefix-parse 6%, kv-cache 10% (cache churn observed), model-infer 52%, batcher-wait 22%, emit/egress 3%
- Observation: higher kv-cache misses when long-run traffic increases; model-infer variance large (kernel scheduling preemption visible in traces).

Cohort: long (129-512) - 15% of traffic
- E2E p50: 420ms, p95: 980ms, p99: 2.1s
- Per-stage fraction (p95 sample): tokenization 6%, prefix-parse 4%, kv-cache 28% (heavy misses and cold starts), model-infer 48%, batcher-wait 9% (batches often size 1), emit/egress 5%
- Observation: long requests cause KV-cache eviction waves for pinned models; also increases memory pressure leading to slower kernel selection.

Cohort: streaming/chunked - 5% of traffic
- E2E p50: N/A (streams measured per-chunk), chunk p95: 180ms, chunk p99: 450ms
- Per-chunk stage breakdown: small model-infer + frequent egress; observed backpressure from client and server-side queueing interplay.

Cross-cohort comparisons (key takeaways):
- Batcher-wait is the dominant contributor to p95 for short/medium cohorts when long cohort requests are mixed into the same pool.
- KV-cache miss tail (cold-starts) is the dominant contributor to long-cohort p99s; misses add ~200-800ms depending on sequence-length and cache locality.
- Isolating long requests into dedicated pool reduced short-cohort p95 by ~18% in the test run (thermostat pool B effect).
- Routing to cheaper quantized fallback reduced p99 magnitude but introduced subtle regressions in model-infer variance for streamed responses (quality vs latency tradeoff).

Trace-level examples (abridged):
- trace-20251112-9a1b: medium cohort request (seq_len 96), batcher-wait 230ms (batch size 3), kv-cache miss -> model-infer 320ms, total 640ms. Kernel scheduling showed preemption by large long-cohort job at timestamp 2025-11-12T18:23:12Z.
- trace-20251114-f72e: short cohort (seq_len 18), coalesced into batch size 8 normally, but mixed with 2 long requests caused batch flush at 150ms threshold resulting in p95 spike.

Hypotheses generated:
1) Adaptive batching threshold currently uses global 150ms flush — when long-seq requests enter pool they push effective wait times higher for short requests. Proposal: make flush policy cohort-aware or use per-cohort timers.
2) KV-cache eviction policy tuned for overall memory footprint not cohort locality. Proposal: add sequence-length aware pinning and LRU windows per-cohort.
3) Scheduler preemption for kernel selection under GPU contention leads to increased model-infer tail. Proposal: add co-scheduling constraints and priority hints for short-cohort batches.

Quick mitigation experiments (planned / in-progress):
- E1: Spin up 'short-specialized' pool (2x small GPUs with per-cohort timer 50ms) and route 75% of short traffic there. Metric: p95 short <= 300ms within 1 hour of rollout. (Run: staged canary)
- E2: Implement cohort-aware flusher prototype (config flag) in batcher v0.9.2 and run A/B across 2% of traffic for 24h.
- E3: Adjust KV cache LRU window and add seq_len pin on hot keys in gateway to reduce cross-eviction. Roll for 4-hour trial.

Risks / caveats:
- Measurement noise from producer-side SDK timings vs server-side observed times; we attempted to use server-traced timestamps but some external customers' SDKs reframe timestamps.
- Isolating long runs may increase cost; need finance estimate if we keep dedicated long pool ongoing.
- Fallback quantized models reduced latency but some unit tests show token-level quality degradation; run regressions on eval-suite before broad rollout.

Action items / owners:
- Maya: run E1 canary (short-specialized pool) and capture 2h, 24h metrics (owner: Maya) - due 2025-11-21.
- Ravi: prototype cohort-aware flusher PR and perf microbench on bench infra (PR link in linked_artifacts) - due 2025-11-25.
- Ana: KV-cache tuning test plan and memory cost calc; coordinate with infra for capacity (owner: Ana) - due 2025-11-22.
- Connor: add dashboard tile (Console) for cohort-level p50/p95/p99 and per-stage stack breakdown; add alert if short-cohort p95 increases by >20% from baseline.

Open questions and followups:
- How does this generalize to Dedicated/Private deployments where infra shapes differ? Need small cross-env replay to validate.
- Should SLO thermostat be an automated routing policy (moving traffic between pools based on short-term quantiles) or remain an ops knob? Tradeoffs: automation speed vs complexity and potential oscillation.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider adding tiny predictive model to batcher which uses seq_len_estimate to assign a departure deadline per-request.
- We should capture a small micro-benchmark that simulates 20% long, 80% short with spikes to confirm eviction behavior reproducibly.

Attachments / artifacts:
- GH PR with instrumentation and sample csvs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- JIRA: INF-2487 (incident + experiment tracker)
- Raw CSV results uploaded to drive folder: /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/experiments/slo-thermostat/ (see linked csv file names in GH PR)

Status: experiment data collected; initial E1 canary in-progress (started 2025-11-19 14:00 UTC). Next update after 24h canary.

End of notes.
